newsitem.title: FINLAND: FOCUS - Neste plunges to eight-month loss. [CORRECTED 14:33 GMT]
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Neste plunges to eight-month loss. [CORRECTED 14:33 GMT]

text.p: A $100 million write-off on crude oil trading derivatives helped propel Finnish oil group Neste Oy to a shock January-August loss, but the company said on Friday it should end the year in profit.

Reporting a loss before extraordinaries and tax of 26 million markka ($5.7 million), compared with a 1.14 billion profit in January-August 1995, Neste said it had also been hit by weak petrochemicals and lower gains from fixed assets sales.

It made a 2.61 markka loss per share against a 6.63 markka profit in the year-ago period. Net sales fell to 27.65 billion from 29.91 billion. But at the operating level, it made a small profit of 341 million markka against 1.71 billion.

Neste said the loss included a 495 million markka write-down on crude oil derivatives trading to end-August 1997. It had warned on July 25 that sharply rising crude oil prices would cost it around 285 million to end-1996 at that day's prices but has given no details of the contracts that went wrong.
No analysts polled before the result had forecast a loss for the company, which is majority state-owned.
Neste stock was marked down quite sharply in early Helsinki trading, but later improved as some analysts welcomed the decisive write-down. By around midday the shares were up 1.00 at 93.00 markka.
"I assume now the slate is clean for 1997," said Jussi Hyoty, analyst at AG Private Bankers.

Since many analysts had only factored in the 285 million loss Neste announced in July, they said they would likely start by cutting about a third from 1996 estimates which had been around 600 million markka.
Neste said it had now sealed contracts to eliminate risks linked to the complex derivatives contracts maturing by the end of this year and cancelled similar instruments due in 1997 and 1998.
"Neste's remaining unmatured buying and selling contracts are conventional positions, which are considerably smaller in volume than the company's own crude oil production," said Neste's report.

Chief executive Jaakko (corrects from Juha) Ihamuotila told a news conference that Neste's loss was now limited and could even shrink because any further rise in crude oil prices would benefit the company.
"If crude oil prices later rise ... our own crude oil production is substantially larger than these trading volumes, so we would benefit more from a rise ... than we would suffer," he said.

The company -- Finland's largest by sales until the merger of forestry giants UPM and Kymmene last year -- built up considerable oil trading muscle in the 1970s and 1980s as an outlet for barter crude oil from the former Soviet Union.
Last month the company replaced the head of its trading unit and pledged to tighten up its trading procedures.
Neste also said its own industrial performance had improved, with exploration and production strengthening. The unit doubled operating profit to 245 million markka from 121 million.
"We can anticipate that Neste's performance during the last four months of the year will improve," Neste said.

"The group's overall result before extraordinary items for 1996 will be profitable, albeit substantially poorer than in 1995." Its 1995 profit before extras and tax was 1.36 billion markka. ($1=4.57 Markka)
